specific_objectives: 11.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to describe the various types of propellers, principles of operation and pitch change mechanisms.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of CSU cutaway model diagrams; Safety: Do not touch moving parts; Supervision: Instructor monitors diagram interpretation.
intro_questions: What is the primary function of a propeller?
How does a fixed-pitch propeller differ from a variable-pitch propeller?
Why is a Constant Speed Unit required for efficient flight?

development.content:
Types of Propellers
Fixed Pitch Propeller
Variable Pitch Propeller
Hydrodynamic Principles
Blade Angle Definitions

CSU Internal Mechanism
Governor Operation
Oil Pressure Control
Flyweight Centrifugal Force
Pitch Change Sequence

High Pitch vs Low Pitch
RPM Regulation
Throttle vs Mixture
CSU Failure Modes
System Limitations

summary_questions: Explain how the governor maintains constant RPM during flight.
Describe the mechanism that changes propeller pitch in response to oil pressure.
Identify two common failure modes of a Constant Speed Unit.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on the effect of propeller rotation on aircraft and methods used to counteract it, as covered in LP 05.
